b2-urbanusnepi-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Village Sociographers
b2-urbanusnepi-01.scenario: At a bookshop evening in Budapest, a visiting student asks you what the village sociographers of the 1930s set out to do.
b2-urbanusnepi-01.prompt: Tell her what they investigated and how they worked, and set that against the official picture of the countryside.
cues: Contrast the official picture with reality
b2-urbanusnepi-01.target: A falukutatók a szegényparasztság helyzetét tárták fel helyszíni megfigyeléssel és adatokkal. Egyes értelmezések szerint a propaganda idilli falvakat mutatott, holott az uradalmi cselédek nyomorban éltek.
b2-urbanusnepi-01.english: The village sociographers uncovered the situation of the poor peasantry through field observation and data. According to some interpretations, propaganda showed idyllic villages, whereas in fact the estate servants lived in misery.
b2-urbanusnepi-01.canDo: I can explain the aims and methods of the 1930s Hungarian village sociography (falukutatás) movement.

b2-urbanusnepi-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Journal Szép Szó
b2-urbanusnepi-02.scenario: In a Budapest café, a student of literature asks you what the journal Szép Szó and its circle stood for.
b2-urbanusnepi-02.prompt: Tell her who edited the journal and where its writers looked for the key to renewal, while admitting that they saw the misery of the villages.
cues: Admit that they saw the misery of the countryside
Say where they looked for the solution
b2-urbanusnepi-02.target: A Szép Szót többek között József Attila szerkesztette. Az urbánus szerzők jól látták a vidék nyomorát, jóllehet a megoldást a polgári demokráciában keresték.
b2-urbanusnepi-02.english: Attila József was among the editors of Szép Szó. The urbanist writers clearly saw the misery of the countryside, although they sought the solution in bourgeois democracy.
b2-urbanusnepi-02.canDo: I can describe what the urbanist writers around the journal Szép Szó stood for.

b2-urbanusnepi-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Where the Two Camps Differed
b2-urbanusnepi-03.scenario: At a seminar in Budapest, a student asks you where the populist and urbanist camps agreed and where they parted ways.
b2-urbanusnepi-03.prompt: Tell her what many on both sides thought of the large-estate system and what each camp expected for renewal.
cues: Say what many on both sides thought of the estates
b2-urbanusnepi-03.target: A két tábor sok képviselője elviselhetetlennek tartotta a nagybirtokrendszert, csakhogy a népiek a parasztság felemelésétől várták a megújulást, az urbánusok viszont a polgárság politikai emancipációját sürgették.
b2-urbanusnepi-03.english: Many representatives of both camps considered the large-estate system unbearable, except that the populists expected renewal from the uplift of the peasantry, whereas the urbanists urged the political emancipation of the bourgeoisie.
b2-urbanusnepi-03.canDo: I can say where the populist and urbanist camps agreed and where they clashed in the 1930s.

b2-urbanusnepi-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Meeting at Monor
b2-urbanusnepi-04.scenario: At a history museum in Budapest, a visitor asks you about the Monor meeting of June 1985.
b2-urbanusnepi-04.prompt: Tell him who invited the participants, where they met and what the two groups did.
cues: Say that the authorities counted on division, in contrast to what happened
b2-urbanusnepi-04.target: Donáth Ferenc meghívta az értelmiségieket egy Monor melletti erdei kempingbe. A hatalom megosztottságra számított, ezzel szemben a résztvevők nyíltan beszéltek egymással.
b2-urbanusnepi-04.english: Ferenc Donáth invited the intellectuals to a forest campsite near Monor. The authorities counted on division; in contrast to this, the participants spoke openly with each other.
b2-urbanusnepi-04.canDo: I can say who met at Monor in June 1985 and what they discussed.

b2-urbanusnepi-05.title: Communicative Challenge: After 1989
b2-urbanusnepi-05.scenario: At an evening on public life in Budapest, a guest asks you how the old populist and urbanist labels returned after 1989.
b2-urbanusnepi-05.prompt: Tell him which two organisations are linked to the two traditions and what some authors say about the two traditions today.
cues: Name the two organisations and the tradition of each
Say what some authors say about the two traditions
b2-urbanusnepi-05.target: A Magyar Demokrata Fórumot a népi-nemzeti, a Szabad Demokraták Szövetségét ellenben az urbánus-liberális hagyományhoz kötik. Egyes szerzők szerint a két hagyomány együtt alkotja a magyar önismeret egészét.
b2-urbanusnepi-05.english: The Hungarian Democratic Forum is linked to the populist-national tradition, the Alliance of Free Democrats, by contrast, to the urbanist-liberal one. According to some authors, the two traditions together form the whole of Hungarian self-understanding.
b2-urbanusnepi-05.canDo: I can describe how the old populist and urbanist labels came back into Hungarian public debate after 1989.

b2-urbanusnepi-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Short History of the Debate
b2-urbanusnepi-consolidation.scenario: At a conference in Budapest, a student asks you for a short history of the populist-urbanist debate.
b2-urbanusnepi-consolidation.prompt: Tell her what each camp held important in the 1930s and what happened at Monor in 1985.
cues: Say what the populists held important
Say what the urbanists held important
b2-urbanusnepi-consolidation.target: A harmincas években a népi írók a falut, az urbánusok ellenben a polgári demokráciát tartották fontosnak. Monoron 1985-ben a két irányzat képviselői hosszú idő után nyíltan beszéltek egymással.
b2-urbanusnepi-consolidation.english: In the 1930s the populist writers held the village important, the urbanists, by contrast, bourgeois democracy. At Monor in 1985 representatives of the two currents spoke openly with each other after a long time.
b2-urbanusnepi-consolidation.canDo: I can sum up the populist-urbanist debate from the 1930s to the Monor meeting of 1985.
